paragraphs.text: In the last movement the feeling itself changes. Love and landscape get reframed as the poets skill, not just loves own doing. Clouds thunder and travelers start longing; sorrow grows and does not stop. Lovers honor the love-festival, and the clouds arrival — dear friend — they bring it on. Then the tribute: may I be conquered by whichever poet does this with yamakas, those echoing sound-twists. To him I pour water — in a broken pot. A potsherd.

So the abiding love-feeling resolves into something else: the poets own delight in his craft. And the potsherd is both things at once: the vessel the water is poured in, and the namesake the whole poem is named for. It names itself at its close.
